evidence_quotes.quote: To understand the disparity within the urban areas, the study selected two urban slums, one with severe drinking water shortage (Vizhinjam, India) and the other with sufﬁcient drinking water (Barten Hill Colony, India) in the Thiruvananthapuram district (Figure 1).

The study also used the chi-square test, independent t-test and Mann–Whitney U test to compare the variables under each dimension of the water and sanitation deprivation index of households in the two urban slums.
There is a signiﬁcant difference in the average preference for the primary source of drinking water (PSDW) used by households in the two slums (t(200) = 12.45, p = 0.000).

raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Two-slum geographic comparisons (Vizhinjam n = 110 vs. Barten Hill n = 92, total N = 202): primary source of drinking water t(200) = 12.45, p = 0.000 (p. 9); daily water consumption 410 L vs. 349.8 L, t(200) = 3.63, p < 0.05 (p. 9); distance to source 1.85 km vs. 0.195 km, t(200) = 12.245, p = 0.000 (p. 10); collection time 29.3 min vs. 1.69 min, t(200) = 16.42, p < 0.05 (p. 10); monthly water tariff/expenditure INR 616.5 vs. INR 167.98, t(200) = 8.34, p < 0.05 (p. 10); taste satisfaction Mann-Whitney U = 2513, p = 0.000 (Table 2, p. 10); latrine location chi-square(2) = 7.853, p < 0.05 (p. 10); toilet lacking piped water 51.8% vs. 29.3%, chi-square(1) = 10.41, p < 0.01 (p. 11); Alkire-Foster aggregate deprivation index Mo = 0.42 vs. 0.23 at k = 0.4 (Table 6, p. 14, descriptive index only).
raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 4 May 2023 in Sustainability 2023, Vol. 15, Issue 9, Article 7559 (Received 4 February 2023; Revised 10 April 2023; Accepted 27 April 2023).
raw_response.rationale: Although the paper reports inferential bivariate tests (independent two-sample t-tests, chi-square tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests on N = 202 households), every statistical test solely compares two purposively selected slum neighborhoods within Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation—Vizhinjam (n = 110, chosen for severe drinking water shortage) versus Barten Hill Colony (n = 92, chosen for sufficient drinking water)—both of which sit under the same municipal and Kerala Water Authority (KWA) public piped-supply regime. No inferential test evaluates a legal, tenure, formal-recognition, tariff-rule, regulatory, enforcement, or institutional/ownership exposure (house ownership and BPL shares are reported only as baseline slum demographics, and reliance on private tankers in Vizhinjam is driven by perceived water taste rather than legal exclusion or utility ownership policy). Thus, the tested exposure-outcome pairs fail narrow Criterion 2 and fit no SWiM family.
